q: What is the main idea of the passage?

choices.A: Administrative regulations prohibit the use of RPA.
choices.B: RPA is completely replacing human workers in offices.
choices.C: Training is the only challenge in implementing RPA.
choices.D: RPA improves office productivity by automating routine administrative tasks.

passage:
Passage 1 (Questions 1 - 5)
The rise of robotic process automation (RPA) in office management has transformed how
administrative tasks are handled. By automating routine and repetitive tasks such as document
archiving, data entry, and record management, organizations can significantl y increase
productivity. Employees who previously spent hours on manual filing can now focus on
complex problem - solving and strategic planning. However, the implementation of RPA requires
careful system analysis to ensure that the automated workflows align   with existing
administrative regulations. Furthermore, staff members need adequate training to monitor and
maintain these new systems, highlighting a shift in necessary office skills rather than a complete
replacement of human workers.

documents and their understanding of administrative procedures. A successful auditor must be

resource allocation.

passage:

Effective document management is crucial for any modern organization. With the
transition from physical paperwork to digital archives, companies must implement robust
systems to ensure data security and easy retrieval. Archival procedures dictate how long  certain
records must be kept and when they can be legally destroyed. Proper categorization and
tagging of electronic files prevent information from becoming lost in vast digital storage spaces.

minimizes the risk of data breaches and ensures that the organization complies with privacy
laws.
